# hcifootprint — LLM-facing API surface

> Agents and humans: this single page is meant to be read INSTEAD of the source. It is
> verified against the code; where a claim cites a source file, that file is the authority.
> Package: `hcifootprint`. Beta, pre-1.0. Zero-dependency core.

## What this is

hcifootprint turns a web app's interaction surface into a typed, traversable **skill graph**
an LLM agent can plan over and act on — as the signed-in user, through the app's own buttons
and handlers. You author a navigation tree in your own vocabulary (pages, containers, tools);
the library derives the agent-facing skill graph, gates every action on a serializable guard,
and records each occurrence in a footprintjs commit log. Nothing is hidden silently: anything
the runtime derives rather than observes is stamped with an honesty marker, and every refused
action returns a typed reason. It is not tied to any agent framework — you get a fixed
MCP-shaped tool surface any host can drive.

---

## 1. Authoring — `buildNavigationGraph` (canonical, D18)

`buildNavigationGraph(id, def)` validates and freezes one object literal in a single call (no
`.build()`). Node names in the literal become a typed path union, so a typo in a later
`registerToolGroup('catalog.filtr-rail')` is a COMPILE error, not a silent no-op.

Source: `src/tree/appmap.ts`, `src/tree/types.ts`.

```ts
import { buildNavigationGraph } from 'hcifootprint';

const graph = buildNavigationGraph('shop', {
  pages: {
    catalog: {
      tools: {
        'search':      { does: 'Search dresses by name or color' },
        'add-to-cart': { does: 'Add the open dress to the cart', when: { authenticated: { eq: true } } },
      },
    },
    checkout: {
      modals: {
        'confirm-order': { tools: { 'place-order': { does: 'Place the order', confirm: true } } },
      },
    },
  },
  skills: {
    purchase: { does: 'Buy a dress end to end', steps: ['add-to-cart', 'place-order'] },
  },
});
```

Authoring vocabulary (all optional except where noted):

- `pages` (REQUIRED) — top-level route targets. Each page is a container node.
- Container buckets inside any node: `areas` (coexist, AND), `tabs` (at most one shown),
  `modals` (overlay; a shown blocking modal masks sibling tools — `blocks: false` = popover).
- `tools` — leaf actions on a node. A tool's fields (source: `ToolDef`, `src/tree/types.ts`):
  - `does` (REQUIRED) — one authored sentence; it is BOTH your label and the tool description
    the LLM reads. It is a source-code literal, never runtime text (injection firewall).
  - `when` — availability guard (a flat WhereFilter; see §4). AND-composed with every ancestor `when`.
  - `enabledWhen` — is it CLICKABLE right now? A different question from `when`: a failed `when`
    HIDES the tool, a false `enabledWhen` SERVES it greyed out (`enabled: false` on the edge) and
    refuses a fire as `TOOL_DISABLED` (retriable). Declare it from the same expression that renders
    `<button disabled={…}>`. NOT composed with ancestor `when`s. Keys it cannot evaluate never
    disable anything — the library does not guess a control greyed out.
  - `writes` — state keys this tool claims to change (verified at settlement).
  - `verify` — the app's OWN check that firing really did something, evaluated at settlement. Either
    a WhereFilter over projected state (`{ 'wizard.recipe': { ne: '' } }`) or a SYNCHRONOUS predicate
    `(state) => boolean` handed a DETACHED snapshot (its closure may read the app's own DOM). If it
    does not hold, the settlement is `effectStatus: 'refused'` — an existing word — instead of the
    'performed' a handler earns merely by returning. What it cannot evaluate (an unknown key, a
    predicate that threw) is `verifyHeld: 'unevaluable'`, never a refusal.
  - `goTo` — page id this tool claims to navigate to.
  - `confirm` — high-effect gate: requires explicit confirmation before firing.
  - `input` — payload contract (Zod, JSON Schema, any `.safeParse`/`.parse` validator) — or the
    literal `'none'`, meaning this control takes NO input. A caller that sends one anyway is refused
    `PAYLOAD_INVALID` with the shape it sent, and a blank payload (`undefined`, `''`, `{}`) is erased
    before it can reach the handler and override the app's own defaults. OMITTING `input` says
    something different: the library does not know the shape, so it advertises nothing.
  - `binding` — how to reach it on screen (ARIA role + name first); optional (handlers don't need it).
- Root-level `tools` (multi-attach): a tool offered on several pages, each entry needs `on: string | string[]`.
- `skills` — named multi-step flows. Fields (source: `JourneyDef`): `does` (REQUIRED planner text),
  `steps` (REQUIRED, tool ids by qualified path or unambiguous suffix), `when` (precondition guard).
- `repeats: true` on a container = a template (one parameterized tool for N cards). Optional
  `instances: (state) => string[]` is the complete instance set; without it, served lists fall
  back to the mounted window (marked `enumeration: 'mounted-window'`).

Returns a `NavigationGraph` (source: `src/tree/types.ts`): `{ id, spec, nodes, toolNodes,
createSession(opts?), requiredStateKeys() }`. All referential/shape mistakes (unknown `goTo`,
guard-operator typos, ambiguous skill steps, contradictory ancestor/descendant guards) throw at
build time.

**v1 `skillGraph()` is legacy sugar.** The fluent `skillGraph('id').page(...).affordance(...).build()`
builder (source: `src/graph/builder.ts`) still ships and works, but `buildNavigationGraph` is the
canonical authoring surface — it adds the container tree (modals/tabs/repeats), typed node paths,
and mount-time tool declaration. Prefer it for new work.

---

## 2. Session lifecycle

`graph.createSession(opts?)` returns an `InteractionSession`. Source: `src/traverse/nav-session.ts`
(runtime), `src/traverse/session.ts` (base), `src/atom/types.ts` (result types).

### `createSession(opts)` — `InteractionSessionOptions`

Extends the base `SessionOptions` (source: `src/atom/types.ts`) plus two tree-only fields.

- `node?: string` — starting page id. Default: the first declared page.
- `state?: Record<string, unknown>` — initial projected state (the lean snapshot guards read —
  not your whole app store).
- `stateTap?: boolean` — whether this session receives `updateState()` reports. Default: true when
  `state` was provided, else false. Without a tap, declared-writes fires settle on handler
  completion (or immediately) with `effectVerified: 'unobservable'` instead of pending forever.
- `redactedKeys?: string[]` — keys stored as `'REDACTED'` in the commit log; live state keeps raw values.
- `commitValues?: 'full' | 'delta'` — commit-log value encoding (footprintjs dial). Default `'delta'`.
- `onWarn?: (message: string) => void` — dev-warning sink (StrictMode re-registrations, handler
  errors, sensor drift). Default `console.warn`.
- `captureProduced?: boolean` — capture each handler's RETURN value onto its transition
  (`produced`, sanitized + capped) as the "act → get data back" channel. Default true.
- `allowUnmaterializedFires?: boolean` — let AGENT fires of declared-but-UNBOUND tools proceed as
  honest no-ops (`executed: false` + `materialized: false` on the result, an `unmaterialized-fire`
  gap row, `materialized: false` stamped on every served edge) instead of the default
  `NOT_MATERIALIZED` rejection. For guide/tour/plan flows. Default false (fail-closed).
- `requireHumanApproval?: boolean | { expiresAfterMs?: number; refuseWhenWorldMoved?: boolean }` —
  refuse a high-effect AGENT fire unless it carries `FireOptions.askId`, a pointer to a confirm-journal
  row a person's own control recorded (`approveAsk`), or a standing `alwaysApprove` grant. Without it
  `confirm: true` is the agent's own request to proceed and authorizes nothing by itself. Default absent
  (fail-closed, byte-identical). Both staleness rules default off — the stamps are always recorded.
- `dormantGraceMs?: number` — how long a registration outside the router-confirmed page may
  persist before drift telemetry fires. Default 3000ms.
- `now?: () => number` — the clock the grace timers and the confirm chain read (epoch ms). Default
  `Date.now`. Inject a controllable clock for deterministic staleness tests.

### `registerToolGroup(path, opts?)` — `RegisterToolGroupOptions`

Call when a component that renders `path` mounts. You NEVER name a group — this returns a
`ToolGroupHandle` that IS the identity; hold it and call `.unregister()` on unmount. `path` is
typed against the graph's node paths. Source: `src/traverse/nav-session.ts`.

Options:

- `handlers?: Record<string, ToolHandler>` — bind the app's EXISTING functions (by reference) to
  tools declared on this node. `ToolHandler = (payload?) => unknown | Promise<unknown>`.
- `tools?: Record<string, RegisteredToolDef>` — declare NEW leaf tools here-and-now (the
  register-with-just-a-description path). `RegisteredToolDef` = a `ToolDef` plus an optional `handler`.
- `instance?: string` — instance key when registering one card of a `repeats` container (e.g. `'o-123'`).
- `visible?: boolean` — initial visibility signal (same wire as `setVisible`).
- `enabled?: Record<string, boolean>` — initial per-tool enabled state (grey a button out; flip
  later via `handle.setEnabled(toolId, false)`).
- `busy?: Record<string, string>` — which controls are ALREADY WORKING as this mounts, in the app's
  OWN WORDS (`{ save: 'Saving your draft…' }`); flip later via `handle.setBusy(toolId, label)` and
  clear with `undefined`. A LABEL, never a flag: there is no boolean form, a non-string is refused
  with one warning, and a tool absent from the map says NOTHING about that control (never "idle").
  It gates nothing — a busy control that is not disabled still fires — and no clock in this library
  ever expires it. A live store says the same thing through `LiveAction.busy`.

Returns `ToolGroupHandle`: `{ id, node, instance?, setEnabled(toolId, enabled),
setBusy(toolId, busy), unregister() }`. `registerTool(path, toolId, { handler, ... })` is the
single-tool convenience form (its `ToolHandle` carries `setEnabled(enabled)` / `setBusy(busy)`).

### Reporting reality — fire / updateState / sync / stimulus

- `fire(affordanceId, opts)` — apply a transition. `opts` (`FireOptions`): `source` (Principal:
  `'user' | 'agent' | 'system' | 'unknown'`), `payload?`, `instance?`, `expectedVersion?`
  (optimistic-concurrency token from `available().version`), `invoke?` (default true; false =
  record-only, for a DOM sensor, or an external actuator that already executed the action),
  `askId?` (the confirm-journal row authorizing this fire — read only under `requireHumanApproval`;
  a POINTER, never a secret). **There is no `confirm` field on `FireOptions` and there will not
  be**: a boolean the caller controls is not evidence. `confirm` is a MODE B TOOL ARGUMENT, so a
  fire reaching the session directly is not gated by it at any layer — the app's own code owns its
  session. `requireHumanApproval` keys on the PRINCIPAL rather than the door, so an agent-sourced
  high-effect fire is held wherever it comes from, including this call.
  Returns `FireResult` — `{ ok: true, transition, version, settlement: 'settled' | 'awaiting-state',
  executed?: false, materialized?: false }` or a typed `{ ok: false, reason, ... }` (see §6).
  **An agent fire of a tool nothing is bound to is refused `NOT_MATERIALIZED`** — firing it would
  execute nothing. The app self-report tier (`source: 'user' | 'system'`, or `invoke: false`) is
  never gated: that motion really happened. A session created with `allowUnmaterializedFires` lets
  the no-op through and marks it `executed: false` + `materialized: false` instead. The success arm
  also carries `effectStatus` (the INVOCATION axis at return time — never `'performed'` there,
  because the handler is always deferred) and `whenSettled` (a promise resolving ONCE with the final
  truth; it NEVER rejects — a refusal arrives as data).
- `settlementOf(transitionId)` → `Promise<FireSettlement>` — the same final truth for anyone holding
  the id (a relay, a poll, a later tool call), long after the fire came to rest. Same laws as
  `whenSettled`: one answer, first settlement wins, never rejects, and a fire the app never reports
  on stays OPEN (a timed-out answer could only be a guess). `settlementIfKnown(transitionId)` is the
  same answer WITHOUT waiting — `undefined` while the question is open. Both THROW synchronously on
  an unknown id or a stimulus/sync row, naming the fires that are live; a promise nobody can ever
  resolve is the failure they exist to prevent.
- `pending()` → `PendingInfo[]` `{ id, affordanceId, firedAt }` — fires still awaiting the app's
  state report (the non-blocking door).
- `awaitingSettlement()` → `string[]` — the ids whose settlement question is still OPEN, in fire
  order. NOT the same list as `pending()`: a fire declaring no writes never joins that one while its
  handler runs, so `pending()` alone answers "nothing is live" about an action that is running.
  Every pending fire is awaiting a settlement; not every fire awaiting a settlement is pending.
- `beginWork(label?, { transitionId? })` → `WorkHandle` `{ workId, done(error?) }` — THE WORK LEDGER:
  the app says it is working on something and hands back the only thing that closes the row. Pair it
  like a lock (`beginWork` in the `try`, `done()` in the `finally`). Binding is by CALL PATH and is
  decided at call time: the `transitionId` you name, else the fire whose handler you are inside
  BEFORE its first `await`, else UNBOUND at principal `'system'` with one dev warning (never a guess
  at "the newest fire"). `done()` closes the row and settles NOTHING — not even `done(error)`, which
  is recorded on the work row only; the failure spine stays a handler throw, a returned `{ok:false}`,
  or `reject()`. It bumps no version, so bookkeeping can never make a plan stale.
- `openWork()` → `WorkRow[]` `{ workId, label?, transitionId?, affordanceId?, startedAt, principal }`
  — the app's OPEN work, oldest first (copies). The third "what is still live?" door: a fire comes to
  rest when the app reports its delta while the app may keep working, and `pending()` /
  `awaitingSettlement()` both answer "nothing" about that window. Every row is the APP'S CLAIM —
  nothing here verifies, measures or ends it, and NO TIMER expires a row (a leaked handle keeps
  saying "still working" for the session's life, by design). `startedAt` is data; no duration is
  ever rendered from it.
- `updateState(delta, opts?)` — the app reports a projected-state delta (router/store tap); pending
  fires settle. `opts` (`UpdateOptions`): `transitionId?` (settle THIS pending precisely — preferred
  over FIFO), `stimulus?`, `principal?`. Returns `UpdateResult`.
- `sync(observedNode, opts?)` — reconcile the cursor when the world moved without an offered edge
  (back button, redirect, deep link). `opts`: `stimulus?`, `principal?`. An unauthored page is not an
  error — the cursor follows reality and `available()` honestly serves zero edges there
  (`offGraph: true`). `sync` takes a PAGE ID, not a URL: if your router speaks paths, translate with
  `matchRoute(graph.spec.pages, location.pathname) ?? location.pathname` — it reads the `route` each
  page already declared (literal segments + `:param`, trailing-slash / query / hash insensitive,
  most-literal-segments wins) and returns `undefined` rather than guessing, which leaves an
  unplaceable path on the existing off-graph behavior. Source: `src/graph/route-match.ts`.
- **Stimulus** = world-initiated motion (`StimulusKind`: `'navigation' | 'timeout' | 'push' |
  'structure-swap' | 'unknown'`). It is not a standalone method on the session — you record it via
  the `stimulus` option on `updateState`/`sync`. When set, the delta is NEVER attributed to a pending
  fired transition (a server push must not hijack an action's provenance). (`hcifootprint/testing`'s
  harness exposes a convenience `stimulus()` method — source: `src/testing/harness.ts`.)

### Reading + observing

- `available()` → `AvailableSlice` `{ version, node, edges }`. Each edge carries `affordanceId`,
  `description`, `role`, `highEffect`, guard `evidence`, the input contract (`schema?` = the LIVE
  validator, in-process only; `expects?` = the same contract WIRE-shaped — zod normalized, JSON
  Schema detached, a non-serializable validator named in one sentence, `'none'` for an input-less
  action), and honesty stamps: `guardUnevaluated?`, `activation?`, `presence?: 'unknown'`,
  `materialized?`, `enabled?`, `instances?`/`enumeration?`. `expects` is byte-for-byte what Mode B
  serves, from one shared derivation — never re-derive it.
- `availableSkills()`, `contextBrief(opts?)` (token-lean prompt context, authored strings only),
  `explain(id)`, `why(key)` (footprint backward causal slice).
- `groundTruth(opts?)` → `{ node, version, text }` — the AUTHORITATIVE facts block: position, then
  every ATTEMPT and how it came to rest, in plain words ("DID happen", "ran, but the effect was
  unobservable", "did NOT happen — … was refused: TOOL_DISABLED", "not yet known"), then any
  decision the human still owes and any fire the app has not answered. It merges BOTH ledgers, which
  is why it exists: a refused fire is a gap row, NOT a transition, so `contextBrief()` structurally
  cannot show failed attempts. With nothing attempted it says so outright — the anti-narration line
  for a model that would otherwise fill the silence with its own prose. Options:
  `{ sinceVersion?, maxAttempts? }` (default 20). Excludes state values, payloads, produced data,
  available actions (that is `whats_here`'s job) and all interpretation.
- `skillPlan(id)` → the derived dependency DAG with live per-step status; THROWS on an unknown id.
  `trySkillPlan(id)` is the same plan for an id you did not author (a model's, a URL's):
  `{ ok: true, plan }` or `{ ok: false, reason: 'UNKNOWN_SKILL', known }` — the identical failure
  shape `commitSkill()` returns.
- Passive observers: `on('transition' | 'state' | 'structure' | 'gap' | 'confirm', listener)` →
  unsubscribe fn. A throwing listener is isolated, never aborts the session.
- Gap ledger: `gaps()` / `onGap(row => ...)` — every refused fire (`kind: 'fire-rejected'`), every
  explicit `reportGap(...)` (`kind: 'reported'`; pass `actionsMayBeStale: true` when the row also says
  the ACTIONS ON OFFER may be out of date — that mark, and only that, puts an authored line in the
  facts block a model reads), every allowed no-op tour fire
  (`kind: 'unmaterialized-fire'` — the binding still to build), and every page the cursor rests on
  where nothing could be performed at all (`kind: 'dead-end'`) becomes a token-lean, name-only row
  for demand-driven triage. `kind` GROWS release to release; no shipped value ever changes meaning,
  so read a row by the kind you know and let the rest fall through as informational (an exhaustive
  `never` check over today's four is the one shape a future kind will stop compiling).
- Confirm journal (D21): `confirmAsk(id)` → `{ askId, receipts }` (receipts = `willDo` / `because` guard
  evidence / `youAreOn` / `recentSteps`, assembled from live state); `declineConfirm(id, {by?, note?})`;
  `confirms()` / `onConfirm(row => ...)` — the auditable ask→decision→fire chain (a confirmed `fire()`
  auto-closes the ask as `approved` and stamps `TransitionRecord.askId`). SEPARATE from the gap ledger:
  a gated action is consented capability, not unmet demand.
- Enforced approval (opt-in, `requireHumanApproval`): `confirmAsk(id, {source?, input?, instance?})` puts
  the input on the card (`receipts.willUse`); the human's own control calls `approveAsk(askId, {by})` /
  `declineAsk(askId, {by})` / `alwaysApprove(id, {by, instance?, expiresInMs?})` /
  `revokeAlwaysApprove(id, {by})`, all returning a typed `ApprovalResult` (never throwing — they run in
  click handlers) and all stamping `principal: 'user'` with no argument to override it. A high-effect
  agent fire then needs `fire(id, {askId})`; refusals are `APPROVAL_REQUIRED` / `_SPENT` / `_MISMATCH`
  (with `differs`) / `_STALE` / `_DECLINED`, each landing BOTH a `'fire-rejected'` gap row and a
  `'refused'` confirm row. `ConfirmRecord.kind` grows by `'always-approved' | 'used' | 'refused' |
  'revoked'`. One yes = one fire (a replay is `APPROVAL_SPENT`); an ALWAYS ALLOW is scoped to the action,
  never to the input, and every exercise lands a `'used'` row. The gate keys on the PRINCIPAL: a direct
  `session.fire(id, {source:'agent'})` is gated; `source: 'user'`/`'system'` and the record-only sensor
  (`invoke:false`) are the app-self-report tier and are not — so `skillsAsTools(session, {source:'user'})`
  is a port whose fires are NOT gated: it warns when built and serves the unenforced `confirm`/`decline`
  descriptions (`session.requiresHumanApprovalFrom(principal)` is the honest question for a port,
  `requiresHumanApproval` the one about the session). The ask binds a detached COPY of the input, so
  mutating your own object after the yes is `APPROVAL_MISMATCH`, not a match. Under enforcement
  `declineConfirm` records a REPORT and closes nothing whatever `principal` it is handed (the row is
  marked `relayed`); the human's no is `declineAsk(askId, {by})`, which outranks a standing grant for
  the action+instance+input the person was shown, with or without the pointer.

---

## 3. Mode B serving — `skillsAsTools`

`skillsAsTools(session, opts?)` projects the session as a FIXED set of MCP-shaped tools whose bytes
never change for the life of a conversation (keeps the prompt cache warm). Disclosure rides the
RESULT channel. Source: `src/serve/modes.ts`.

```ts
import { skillsAsTools } from 'hcifootprint';

const port = skillsAsTools(session);            // opts: { confirmHighEffect?: boolean=true, source?: Principal='agent' }
// Leave `source` at 'agent' for any port a MODEL drives. It stamps the principal on every fire the
// port makes, and the NOT_MATERIALIZED guarantee keys off it: a port stamping 'user'/'system' is
// declaring app self-report, so its unbound fires are deliberately NOT gated and the success-shaped
// no-op comes back. Only stamp a non-agent source for a port your own code drives.
const tools = port.tools();                     // static MCPToolDescription[] — register with your host
const result = port.call(name, args);           // route a tool_use; return `result` as the tool_result
```

`tools()` returns, for graph id `shop`:

- one tool per skill: `shop.skill.<id>` (input: `{ step?, input?, confirm?, decline?, instance? }`)
- `shop.whats_here` — describe the current position. Optional `{ sinceVersion }`: pass a version
  from any previous result and the reply narrates only the DELTA since it (who did what since the
  model's last look) — cheaper re-grounding after write-steps.
- `shop.do_action` — perform one available action outside any skill flow (`{ action, input?, confirm?, decline?, instance? }`)
- `shop.why` — the causal backward slice for a state key (`{ key }`)
- `shop.did_it_work` — how an action came to rest (`{ transitionId }`, taken from that action's
  result — or the `askId` from a `needs-confirm` result, to learn whether the human has decided).
  A POLL, never a wait — see §5.

`MCPToolDescription` = `{ name, description, inputSchema }` (source: footprintjs).

### The three call shapes

- **`shop.whats_here` →** `{ ok: true, facts, brief, actions: [{ action, does, goesTo?, holds?,
  enabled?, busy?, highEffect?, guardUnevaluated?, instances?, enumeration?, activation?, expects? }], skills: [{ skill,
  does, feasible, feasibilityUnknownFor? }], youAreOn, version }`. `goesTo?` is the page this edge CLAIMS
  it will move you to (the declared `goTo`; absent when none is declared) — its success evidence is
  PAGE MOTION, because a navigation declares no writes and nothing on the page has to change.
  `holds?` is WHAT THAT CONTROL IS HOLDING RIGHT NOW — the draft already in the box, read when the row
  was served. Use it instead of asking the human to retype what they can see, and never invent one:
  the key is ABSENT whenever the app declared no way to read the value, so absence means the library
  does not know, not that the box is empty. It is a reading, not a binding — firing still sends the
  `input` you pass. `enabled?` appears ONLY as `false` — the app has switched that control off, on
  screen and not clickable (a clickable control carries no key at all); firing it anyway is refused
  `TOOL_DISABLED` with `retriable: true` and a sentence that names the STATE and refuses to invent a
  reason for it, because nothing in this library knows one. `busy?` is the app's OWN LABEL for
  "working on it right now" (`'Saving your draft…'`) — the third state beside clickable and switched
  off. Presence-only again: an absent key means the library does not know, NEVER "not busy". It gates
  nothing (a busy control that is not disabled still fires) and nothing here will ever time it out —
  wait and re-read, or ask `did_it_work` about a fire you already made; do not fire again to find
  out. `expects?` is that action's declared
  input contract (absent when the action declares none; `'none'` when it takes no input) — the same
  shape a `PAYLOAD_INVALID` rejection teaches, and the same value `available()` serves.
  **`facts`** is `groundTruth().text` (see §2): the app's own record of what was ATTEMPTED and how
  each attempt came to rest, under a header declaring it authoritative over anything said in the
  conversation. Trust it over your own memory of the turn — including refused fires, which the
  `brief` cannot show. `{ sinceVersion }` narrows both.
- **`shop.skill.<id>` with no `step` →** opens the skill frame and returns `frameData`:
  `{ ok: true, skill, frame: 'open', judgment, readySteps: [...], laterSteps: [...], howToAct,
  awaitingState?, youAreOn, version }`.
- **`shop.skill.<id>` with `step` →** fires that step: merges `frameData` + `fireData` + position.
- **`shop.do_action` with `action` →** fires one action: `fireData` + position.

### `ServeResult` shape

`ServeResult = Record<string, unknown>` — a plain data object; serialize it as the tool_result body.
Text fields are authored strings only; runtime values (state, payloads, instance keys, evidence,
produced data) are structured DATA fields. Fields you will encounter (source: `src/serve/modes.ts`):

- `ok: boolean` and `judgment` — the routing discriminant on `ok: false`:
  `'blocked'` (skill precondition fails), `'error'` (unknown step/action, bad tool), `'needs-confirm'`
  (high-effect step awaiting `confirm: true` — carries `askId` + `receipts` + `performed: false` + an
  authored `why`: NOTHING has been done and this is a question for the human, not a failure — never
  report it as an error; `decline: true` records the refusal and returns `judgment: 'declined'`),
  `'rejected'` (fire refused — carries `reason`).
  On an open frame `judgment` is `'navigate-or-wait' | 'one-ready-step' | 'needs-choice'`; on
  completion `'done'`.
- Position (always): `youAreOn` (current node), `version` (the total-order cursor).
- Frame: `frame` (`'open' | 'completed' | 'cancelled' | 'demoted'`), `readySteps`
  (`[{ step, does, highEffect?, guardUnevaluated?, materialized?, expects? }]` — `materialized: false`
  means nothing is bound to execute that step), `laterSteps` (`[{ step, status }]`),
  `awaitingState?` (steps whose fire has not yet been reported back), `howToAct`.
- Fire success: `did` (the step id fired), `settlement` (`'settled' | 'awaiting-state'`),
  `effectStatus` (the INVOCATION axis at return time — `'pending'` means nobody has done it YET),
  `howToSettle?` (present only on `'pending'`: the authored pointer at `shop.did_it_work`),
  `transitionId` (fetch `producedFor(id)` after awaiting an async handler), `guardUnevaluated?`,
  `executed?: false` + `materialized?: false` (an allowed unmaterialized tour fire — NOTHING ran),
  `toNodeClaimed?: true` (the cursor moved on the edge's declared `goTo` CLAIM, not on an
  observation — re-`sync()` before trusting `youAreOn`; see §5).
- Fire rejection: `reason` (see §6), plus `evidence?` / `issues?` / `instances?` / `node?` /
  `expects?` / `retriable?` depending on the reason.
- Name not served (`do_action` only): `reason: 'UNKNOWN_ACTION' | 'AMBIGUOUS_ACTION'` + `actions`
  (the ids that ARE served). The port refuses these itself — no `fire()` runs, so they are NOT in
  the gap ledger or `facts`. When the app HAS the asked action (exact id), the refusal adds `why`:
  it is on another page, or on this page with its conditions unmet — then `evidence` (+
  `guardUnevaluated?`) carries the same detail a `GUARD_FAILED` fire does. A name the graph does
  not have gets no `why`: the library does not invent an explanation for something it never saw.

---

## 4. THE GUARD RULES (read before writing a state projector)

Source: `src/graph/guards.ts` (shape + operators), `src/traverse/session.ts` `#evalGuard`
(runtime evaluation).

**A guard is a flat WhereFilter.** `key → { op: value }`. Operators (the ONLY eight):
`eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte, in, notIn` (`in`/`notIn` take an array). The map is evaluated
**AND-only**: every key must match, and multiple ops under one key must ALL hold. There is
**NO `$or`, no nesting, no disjunction of any kind** — the filter is deliberately flat. `{}` (an
empty guard) is rejected at build time because the evaluator never matches an empty filter.

**Absent guard key ⇒ SERVED, not hidden.** At evaluation, keys of the guard that are NOT present in
the projected state are collected as *unevaluable*. Only the evaluable subset decides `matched`. So:

- a guard key **absent** from projected state → the edge is served ANYWAY, carrying the
  `guardUnevaluated: [key, ...]` marker (the condition is flagged as taken-on-faith — the app stays
  the enforcer). It is NOT treated as false, and NOT hidden.
- a guard key **present but failing** its operator → the edge IS hidden (`available()` omits it).
- `undefined` is never stored: a report entry whose value is `undefined` is dropped (a declared
  write reported as `undefined` counts as MISSING), and a key somehow holding `undefined` is as
  unevaluable as an absent one — it rides `guardUnevaluated`, never sneaks past an operator
  (src/traverse/session.ts).

The consequence: an incompletely-seeded projector silently degrades honest availability into
unevaluated-guess territory (everything shows up flagged instead of actually decided).

**Fix: seed every key from `graph.requiredStateKeys()` (see §7).** A projection covering that whole
set is what lets guards actually decide rather than defer.

**The OR pattern — derive a boolean in your projector.** Because the filter is AND-only, you express
disjunction by computing a derived flag in the state you report, then guarding on that flag:

```ts
// "checkout is allowed when the cart has items OR a saved order exists" — AND-only can't express OR,
session.updateState({ canCheckout: cart.length > 0 || savedOrder != null });   // so derive the boolean
// then author the guard as:  when: { canCheckout: { eq: true } }
```

---

## 5. THE SETTLEMENT RULE (agents: re-read after every write-step)

Source: `src/traverse/session.ts` (`fire` / `#settle`), `src/serve/modes.ts` (`frameData`).

A step that declares `writes` does not settle synchronously when a state tap is wired. `fire()`
returns **`settlement: 'awaiting-state'`** and the transition sits **pending** until the app reports
the real delta via `updateState(...)`. Until then:

- the fired step is excluded from `readySteps` (advertising it would tell the model to double-fire),
  and it appears in `awaitingState`;
- any downstream step whose guard depends on that write is NOT `ready` yet — it only becomes ready
  after the app reports state back.

**Therefore an agent MUST re-read `whats_here` (or re-open the skill tool) after any write-step** —
the readySteps in the write-step's own result were computed before the app moved, so they are stale
for what comes next. (When there is no state tap, or the step declares no writes, `fire()` returns
`settlement: 'settled'` immediately and no re-read wait applies — but re-reading is always safe.)

**And to learn whether it actually worked, ASK — never assume.** `effectStatus` on a fire result is the
truth AT RETURN TIME; for anything the app still has to do it is `'pending'` (nobody has done it yet), and
the result names the door out in `howToSettle`. Call `shop.did_it_work` with that `transitionId`. It is a
POLL, so it answers immediately, one of these ways:

- settled — `{ ok: true, settled: true, did, effectStatus, outcome, outcomeNow?, effectVerified,
  writesObserved?, verifyHeld?, arrival?, arrivalMeans?, stillWorking?, stillWorkingMeans?, toNode?,
  error?, data? }`. THREE axes, none averaged into another:
  `effectStatus` = did anyone perform it; `effectVerified` = were the declared writes observed;
  `verifyHeld` = did the app's OWN declared `verify` condition hold (absent when no contract was
  declared — silence, never a passing grade). `'refused'` covers FOUR routes, one word: the handler
  threw, it returned a failure, the app called `reject()`, or the `verify` contract found nothing
  happened — and in that last case `error` carries the contract's own sentence. `writesObserved` is
  the boolean form of `effectVerified` (named for its axis so it can never be read as the contract's
  verdict) and is ABSENT when the answer is not knowable (the string `'unobservable'` would read as
  truthy). A settlement is a RECEIPT and first settlement wins, so the record
  can move afterwards (a server rejecting an already-reported order flips it to `'rolled-back'`); when the
  live record no longer agrees, `outcomeNow` rides ALONGSIDE `outcome` — never over it — with `howToAct`
  saying to check `whats_here` before acting on the receipt. `arrival` rides the same way and appears
  only on an action that declared a navigation: `'claimed'` (the app said it navigates and nothing has
  observed it arrive — including a fire nothing executed, beside `materialized: false`) or `'observed'`
  (a later `sync()` landed on the page it claimed). `arrivalMeans`
  is the authored sentence for whichever one you got. There is NO third value for "did not arrive" —
  a sync elsewhere, or no sync at all, leaves `'claimed'` standing, because a later legitimate hop and
  a failed navigation are indistinguishable from here and a clock is not evidence. `'observed'` is
  corroboration, never proof of cause: the sync row that produced it is still an unverified hop.
- still running — `{ ok: true, settled: false, judgment: 'still-pending', did, howToAct }`. Do NOT perform
  the action again; call again with the same id.
- still WORKING — `stillWorking: true` (plus the authored `stillWorkingMeans`) rides EITHER of the two
  arms above when the app has opened a work row for that fire and not closed it (`beginWork`, §2). On
  the settled arm it sits BESIDE the receipt exactly as `outcomeNow` does: a fire can be at rest while
  the app is still working, and both are true at once. It is the app's own account, not a verdict on
  anything else on the result, no judgment word was minted for it, and NOTHING here will time it out —
  ask again, or re-read `whats_here`; never perform the action again to find out.
- paused (you passed an `askId`) — `{ ok: true, settled: false, performed: false, judgment, askId, did,
  howToAct }`, where `judgment` is `'awaiting-human'` (nobody has decided), `'approved-not-yet-done'`
  (a yes is on record and nothing has fired), `'approval-no-longer-valid'` (a yes is on record and this
  app will not act on it any more — ask again; performing it would be refused forever) or `'declined'`.
  NOTHING was fired, so there is no outcome — and that is not a failure. Once the yes has been SPENT the
  same `askId` answers with the settlement of the fire it authorized. Ids are matched exactly; the
  receipts stay on the ask.
- ambiguous id — `{ ok: false, judgment: 'error', reason: 'AMBIGUOUS_ID', why, askId, askedAbout, did? }`.
  One id named BOTH a fire and a card (an app named an action `ask`, and approval cards are numbered
  `ask#1`, `ask#2`, …). Either answer would be about the other object, so neither is given.
- unknown id — `{ ok: false, judgment: 'error', reason: 'UNKNOWN_TRANSITION', pending: [...],
  awaitingSettlement: [...], awaitingHuman: [{ askId, action }] }`. A wrong id is refused BY NAME, never
  soothed with a "still running" it cannot know. `pending` = fires awaiting the app's STATE report
  (`updateState`'s own word, same meaning); `awaitingSettlement` = every fire this tool can still be
  asked about — the superset, and the one a fire question is about; `awaitingHuman` = the cards a person
  has not answered (asks are not fires, so they join neither of the other two lists).

Over a real MCP server (`mcpServer`) the answer usually arrives without a second call: the server waits up
to `settleWithinMs` (default 250) and spreads EXACTLY what `did_it_work` would answer about that id into
the SAME result — one shared builder, so a folded result and a later poll can never teach two different
things. Where they overlap the settled facts WIN (`'pending'` was true at return time and is not now), and
two fire-time words are DROPPED because the payload no longer describes the moment they were true:
`howToSettle` (it pointed at the poll that just happened) and `settlement` (it answers "does a commit bundle
exist YET?", so leaving it put `'awaiting-state'` beside `writesObserved: true`). Nothing is minted in their
place — `did_it_work` never carried either, so the two doors still agree.
Only a result carrying a `transitionId` is folded at all, and that is an invariant: a `transitionId` is
minted ONLY by an executed fire, so every `needs-confirm`, decline and refusal returns at once with the
ceiling untouched — **an awaited call is structurally incapable of blocking on a person**. Miss the
ceiling and NOTHING is minted: `'pending'` stands, `howToSettle` stays, and no settled field appears.
Keep the ceiling well under the host's own timeout — this server sends no progress notifications, so a
long one just makes the CLIENT error about an action that may well have succeeded; `did_it_work` is the
long-running door. In process, `session.settlementOf(transitionId)` is that truth as a promise,
`session.settlementIfKnown(transitionId)` is it without waiting, and `port.settledAnswer(transitionId)`
is the same facts as a RESULT for a caller holding only the port (`undefined` while in flight, and a
synchronous THROW on an id no settlement can exist for — plus one that names BOTH a fire and a human's open
card, which `did_it_work` refuses as `AMBIGUOUS_ID`); all of them THROW on an id that can never settle.

**And re-`sync()` after any CLAIMED navigation.** A result carrying `toNodeClaimed: true` means the
cursor moved on the graph's declared `goTo` — a claim about your app, not an observation (a bound
handler completing does not confirm it either; only `sync()` does). Confirm the real page with
`session.sync(routerPage)` before trusting `youAreOn`; a mismatch is reconciled and recorded as an
unverified hop instead of silently diverging. That confirmation is also the ONLY thing that can move
`arrival` from `'claimed'` to `'observed'` — and the only thing that re-reads a live action store
(`LiveBindingPort.whenPageChanges`), so an app whose actions come from the router keeps its agent
surface current by syncing. Matching is exact: the page id, or a raw pathname read through the route
table by `matchRoute`'s own segment rules. Never a resemblance.

---

## 6. Typed rejection reasons

`fire()` / Mode B `judgment: 'rejected'` carry one of (source: `FireResult`, `src/atom/types.ts`):
`UNKNOWN_AFFORDANCE`, `STALE_CURSOR`, `NOT_ON_NODE`, `GUARD_FAILED` (with `evidence`),
`PAYLOAD_INVALID` (with `issues` — a wrong shape, or ANY payload sent to an `input: 'none'` action),
`BLOCKED_BY_OVERLAY` (a shown modal masks the node),
`NODE_NOT_VISIBLE`, `STILL_MOUNTING` (RETRIABLE — mounts not arrived yet), `INSTANCE_REQUIRED`,
`INSTANCE_UNKNOWN`, `TOOL_DISABLED` (RETRIABLE — greyed out; four wires reach it: `enabled:` at registration,
`handle.setEnabled`, a live store's `LiveAction.enabled`, and the declarative `ToolDef.enabledWhen`. Carries
`retriable: true` and an authored `why` that names the STATE and refuses to invent a cause — the app switched
it off, and nothing here knows what would change it. Do not guess one; the same fact is served ahead of time
as `enabled: false` on the action row), `NOT_MATERIALIZED` (declared but
unbound — an agent fire would execute nothing; NOT retriable: nothing is en route. Wire it with a
tool group, or create the session with `allowUnmaterializedFires` for read-only touring). Every
refused fire is also a gap-ledger row. **There is no `TOOL_BUSY`, and there will not be**: `busy` is
what the app SAID, not a door it SHUT, so a working control that is not disabled still fires — a
refusal on a control the app also called busy carries the label as data and one authored sentence
BESIDE the refusal's own, never as its cause. High-effect steps return `judgment: 'needs-confirm'` — a PAUSE, not a
failure (`performed: false`: nothing has been done, and the missing piece is a person, not a fix) — so ask the
human, then call again with `confirm: true`. CAPABILITY BEFORE AUTHORITY: a high-effect control the app has
SWITCHED OFF is refused `TOOL_DISABLED` and no card is minted, because nobody may be asked to approve
something nobody can do (`fire()`'s own order, now held on the port's confirm arms too). While they decide, `shop.did_it_work` with that `askId` says
whether they have answered. By default that `confirm: true` is the agent's own request to proceed and is tied to no
recorded decision (an agent that never asks crosses on its first call); create the session with `requireHumanApproval`
and a crossing needs a pointer to an approval the app recorded from a person, or it is refused `APPROVAL_REQUIRED`.

---

## 7. `requiredStateKeys()` — the projector seeding checklist

Present on BOTH graph types (source: `src/graph/builder.ts` for `skillGraph`,
`src/tree/appmap.ts` for `buildNavigationGraph`):

```ts
graph.requiredStateKeys();   // → sorted, deduped string[] of every guard key the graph reads
```

It is the sorted, deduped set of state keys every guard reads — across all tool `when`s,
container-node `when`s (they AND-compose into descendant tools), and skill preconditions — whether
or not the node is currently mounted. Seed each of these keys in your state projector so guards
decide instead of deferring (see §4). This is the one call that closes the guard-honesty loop.

---

## Honesty markers (quick reference)

Everything the runtime DERIVES rather than OBSERVES is flagged, never laundered as fact:
`guardUnevaluated` (guard key absent from state), `activation: 'assumed'` (declared subtree,
nothing registered), `presence: 'unknown'` (ambiguous mounted tabs), `materialized: false`
(declared but no handler wired — on a served edge, and on a fire result together with
`executed: false` when the fire itself ran nothing), `toNodeClaimed: true` (the cursor moved on a
declared `goTo` claim, unconfirmed), `effectVerified: 'unobservable'` (no report to check against),
`verifyHeld: 'unevaluable'` (a declared `verify` contract could not be run — an unknown state key, or a
predicate that threw; never read as a refusal), `enumeration: 'mounted-window'` (instance list is
partial). App text and produced data ride a strict
DATA channel; only authored strings reach the planner's instruction channel.

**Absence is a stance, not an oversight.** `enabled`, `busy`, `holds`, `goesTo` and `stillWorking`
are PRESENCE-ONLY: a key means the app said so, and no key means this library DOES NOT KNOW — never
"clickable", "not busy", "the box is empty" or "finished". A cheerful default on every row would be a
claim about a session nobody was asked about. **And no clock is evidence:** nothing here expires a
`busy` label or a work row, `settleWithinMs` decides how long to wait and never what the answer is,
and a caller who stops waiting reports UNFINISHED — never done, never failed.
